input.question: Why aren’t we allowed to lower the salaries of politicians? So that we can be sure that they are running not for money but because they really want to serve?
input.ground_truth: Mostly because it would become a tool to control the have-nots. Lower the the salaries of politicians until it a burden even for those who want to serve. Net result is that the only people who would run wouldn't be the people who want to serve, but the people who are financially able. Side note. Most of the money politician make come from things other than their salary. Book deals, speeches, etc...

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why aren’t we allowed to lower the salaries of politicians? So that we can be sure that they are running not for money but because they really want to serve?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a lemonade stand, and you and your friends want to take turns running it. If you promise to pay your friends less money every time they help, some friends might only help because they need the money, not because they really like helping you or making lemonade.

If we only let people become leaders (like politicians) because they get a lot of money, then maybe some of them only want the money, not to help everyone. But if we don’t let their pay go down, it’s a little fairer and makes sure that people who really want to help can do it, not just the ones who want the money.

But if we make the pay very low, maybe nobody will want to be a leader, because everyone needs money to live. So, we try to find a way to make sure leaders care about helping people, not just about getting rich. We do this by having rules and watching to make sure they are doing a good job, instead of just changing their salary.
